html:
Batavia was the Dutch port city on the north coast of Java, founded in 1619 as the Asian headquarters of the Dutch East India Company. It later became the capital of the Dutch East Indies and is today Jakarta.

The company's governor general Jan Pieterszoon Coen seized and burned the Javanese port of Jayakarta and built a walled town on its ruins, with canals in the Dutch style. Batavia ran a trading network that stretched from Japan to the Cape, collecting spices, coffee, sugar and textiles. Its people were mostly not Dutch: Chinese traders and craftsmen, Javanese and many enslaved Asians; see Slave trade in Dutch Asia.

In 1740 the colonial authorities and settlers massacred thousands of the city's Chinese; see Batavia massacre. In the 1700s the stagnant canals bred malaria, and the old town became known as a graveyard for Europeans, so the government moved south to newer districts. When Japan occupied the Indies in 1942 the city was renamed Jakarta, and it became the capital of Indonesia after independence.
sum: Batavia was the Dutch port city on the north coast of Java, founded in 1619 as the Asian headquarters of the Dutch East India Company. It later became the capital of the Dutch East Indies and is today Jakarta.
